items.grounds: Re-derived from bytes; every run below collates at byte tier. First-person-singular (1cs) forms run through the verse before the seam: שׂ֧וֹשׂ אָשִׂ֣ישׂ בַּֽיהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier), נַפְשִׁי֙ (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier), בֵּֽאלֹהַ֔י (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier), הִלְבִּישַׁ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier) and יְעָטָ֑נִי (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier) are a 1cs verb and 1cs suffixes; the same utterance continues through the simile כֵּ֣ן אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה יַצְמִ֤יחַ (oshb:Isa.61.11, byte tier), a verse carrying no first-person form at all, and the 1cs voice resumes at the row's own onset in the two lamed-purpose vow clauses לְמַ֤עַן צִיּוֹן֙ לֹ֣א אֶחֱשֶׁ֔ה (oshb:Isa.62.1, byte tier) and וּלְמַ֥עַן יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם לֹ֣א אֶשְׁק֑וֹט (oshb:Isa.62.1, byte tier), both 1cs imperfects. The shipped row's only Hebrew at its front seam is the third-person Zion phrase צִדְקָ֔הּ וִישׁוּעָתָ֖הּ (oshb:Isa.62.1, byte tier) (3fs suffixes), and its only WEB quotation at that verse is the second-half clause “until her righteousness shines out like the dawn, and her salvation like a burning lamp.” (web:Isa.62.1); the resolve clause “For Zion’s sake I will not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not rest,” (web:Isa.62.1) appears in neither witness anywhere in the row, so the row's sole named onset signal is unquoted and unspliced. The row discloses first-person continuity across its rear seam (62:5|62:6) but says nothing about the same continuity across its own front seam, while the book-order neighbor row argues this very seam as a rhetorical-mode shift with the person unchanged. Tested the other way, against the finding: the seam itself is sound, since the report-to-vow shift at the lamed-purpose clauses is real in the bytes, and the paragraph-mark inventory (single witness) carries no parashah mark at MT 61:10, 61:11 or 62:1 (MT 61:11 holds a paseq seg, count-layer only), so the row's no-mark statement is accurate and no tier-3 corroboration is misreported in either direction. The defect is therefore a defective front-seam warrant (its only signal is a feature continuous across the seam, and the feature that does discriminate is unevidenced in the row) plus undisclosed cross-seam person continuity, not a boundary defect: medium as filed.

Re-derived from bytes; every run below collates at byte tier. Second-person-feminine-singular (2fs) address runs unbroken from צִדְקֵ֔ךְ (oshb:Isa.62.2, byte tier), כְּבוֹדֵ֑ךְ (oshb:Isa.62.2, byte tier) and לָךְ֙ (oshb:Isa.62.2, byte tier) through וְהָיִ֛יתְ (oshb:Isa.62.3, byte tier) and אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ (oshb:Isa.62.3, byte tier), בָּ֔ךְ וְאַרְצֵ֖ךְ (oshb:Isa.62.4, byte tier), יִבְעָל֖וּךְ בָּנָ֑יִךְ (oshb:Isa.62.5, byte tier) and עָלַ֖יִךְ אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ (oshb:Isa.62.5, byte tier) into the row's own opening token pair עַל חוֹמֹתַ֣יִךְ (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier) (2fs suffix), after which the vocative יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier) stands as the verse's third token, naming the addressee already under address rather than opening a new one; the first change of addressee inside the row is the second-person-masculine-plural charge אַל דֳּמִ֖י לָכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier), which the row does disclose as intra-span alternation. The row's device_notes nevertheless state that an addressee shift is this unit's own front-seam driver and its signal key names a vocative scene shift, while the book-order neighbor row argues the same seam as marked by no change of addressee, speaker, or person and expressly not on any vocative; the address continuity from MT 62:2 across 62:5|62:6 is disclosed nowhere in this row. Tested the other way, against the finding: the vocative is explicit in the bytes (a tier-1 class where explicit), and the seam survives on the new completed first-person act with a new participant group, הִפְקַ֨דְתִּי֙ שֹֽׁמְרִ֔ים (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier), so the placement stands; the defect is undisclosed cross-seam address continuity together with an addressee-shift framing the bytes do not support, a defective warrant that is not alone load-bearing: medium as filed.

Re-derived from bytes; every run below collates at byte tier. Plural address is already live before the seam: הַמַּזְכִּרִים֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier) identifies the addressees by a participle, and אַל דֳּמִ֖י לָכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier) plus וְאַֽל תִּתְּנ֥וּ (oshb:Isa.62.7, byte tier) are second-person-masculine-plural (2mp) forms. MT 62:10 then carries six 2mp imperatives with no addressee named anywhere in the verse: עִבְר֤וּ עִבְרוּ֙ בַּשְּׁעָרִ֔ים (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier), פַּנּ֖וּ (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier), סֹ֣לּוּ סֹ֤לּוּ (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier), סַקְּל֣וּ (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier) and הָרִ֥ימוּ (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier). The bytes thus establish a content turn (from the charge to give Yahweh no rest to gate, highway and banner commands) under an unbroken 2mp address; they cannot establish that the 62:10 group differs from the 62:6-7 group, which is what the row's ground 'addressed to an unnamed group rather than continuing the charge just laid on the watchmen' asserts. The book-order neighbor row argues the identical seam as 'not a shift to an unnamed addressee but a shift in content' and repeats the rejection in its rejected alternative, so the two rows carry incompatible warrants for one seam, and the neighbor's framing is the one the bytes support. One overstatement in the finding is noted without effect on the verdict: at 62:6 the plural addressees are identified by הַמַּזְכִּרִים֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier) whereas at 62:10 they are not, so the group is in fact more unnamed at 62:10; that is a naming fact, not an addressee change, and the row's warrant still asserts a discontinuity the bytes cannot carry. The seam survives on the doubled verse-initial imperative and the content turn, with a SAMEKH at MT 62:9 in the paragraph-mark inventory (single witness, tier 3), so this is a defective warrant, not a boundary defect: medium as filed.

Re-derived from the shipped row and the bytes. The row's rear-seam sentence carries the Hebrew form-class claim 'a fresh plural-imperative summons' with only the English witness “Go through, go through the gates!” (web:Isa.62.10), which does not mark number; its boundary_evidence_refs pair an oshb entry with every other web verse they cite (62:6, 62:7, 62:8, 62:9 as a setumah entry) but carry no oshb:Isa.62.10, and no Hebrew from that verse appears in any field of the row. The claim itself is byte-true: עִבְר֤וּ עִבְרוּ֙ בַּשְּׁעָרִ֔ים (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier) opens the verse with a doubled 2mp imperative, and the book-order neighbor row splices exactly this run at byte tier for the same seam. Under the engagement-class rule a form-class label on a seam driver is a byte-checkable claim carrying the same discipline as a digit and requiring a pointed splice with its tier named, so a rear-seam driver carried on the English witness alone is an unsupported warrant as shipped rather than a mechanical omission; it is not load-bearing beyond repair because the claim re-derives true and the seam is independently secured by the neighbor row's splice and the SAMEKH at MT 62:9 (single witness, tier 3): medium as filed.

Re-derived from bytes; every run below collates at byte tier. MT 63:6 closes in the first-person singular (1cs): וְאָב֤וּס עַמִּים֙ בְּאַפִּ֔י (oshb:Isa.63.6, byte tier) and וְאוֹרִ֥יד (oshb:Isa.63.6, byte tier) are 1cs verbs with a 1cs suffix. MT 63:7 opens חַֽסְדֵ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אַזְכִּיר֙ (oshb:Isa.63.7, byte tier) with a first-person SINGULAR hiphil imperfect, rendered “I will tell of the loving kindnesses of Yahweh” (web:Isa.63.7); the verse's only first-person-plural element is the object suffix in גְּמָלָ֖נוּ יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.63.7, byte tier), and it contains no first-person-plural verb, so the row's 'a first-person-plural recital of Yahweh's mercies replaces the divine warrior's own first-person report' is byte-false as a person contrast: grammatical person is unchanged across the seam, exactly as the book-order neighbor row states. The row also cites web:Isa.63.7 with no oshb:Isa.63.7 entry and no splice from the verse its rear seam turns on, and ships at confidence high with frontier_flag_considered false. The finding is confirmed as to fact; the filed severity is not. Tested the other way, against the row's own seam: the divine name stands in the third person three times under that 1cs verb, in חַֽסְדֵ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אַזְכִּיר֙ (oshb:Isa.63.7, byte tier), תְּהִלֹּ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.63.7, byte tier) and גְּמָלָ֖נוּ יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.63.7, byte tier), which by itself separates the 63:7 speaker from the warrior who at וְאָב֤וּס עַמִּים֙ בְּאַפִּ֔י (oshb:Isa.63.6, byte tier) reports his own deeds; the speech-act change (recital versus action report) is byte-grounded at the same verb; MT 63:7 carries no interrogative, so the row's 'no further interrogative sustaining the dialogue frame' is byte-true; and the paragraph-mark inventory records a SAMEKH at MT 63:6 (single witness, tier 3; MT 63:7 holds only a count-layer paseq seg). The seam therefore survives with the person-shift descriptor deleted, which the finding's own proposed change concedes ('the seam itself survives on the speech-act change and the tier-3 SAMEKH'). Under the severity law a byte-false claim is high only where it is load-bearing; this descriptor is one of four grounds in the rear-seam sentence and the boundary at 63:6|63:7 does not depend on it, so it is a defective warrant claim not alone load-bearing: downgraded to medium, with the missing oshb:Isa.63.7 engagement and the unrevisited high confidence noted as aggravating but not boundary-affecting.

Re-derived from bytes and the staged crosswalk; every run below collates at byte tier. The row's boundary_rationale writes 'mountains quaking again at 64:2-3' and its strongest_rejected_alternative 'the confessional turn at 64:5' with no witness prefix and no numeric qualifier, inside zone B where the crosswalk maps WEB 64:2, 64:3 and 64:5 to MT 64:1, 64:2 and 64:4. Under the book-wide convention that bare coordinates are WEB, both are content-correct: web:Isa.64.2 (MT 64:1) carries the kindling fire and the trembling nations, כִּקְדֹ֧חַ אֵ֣שׁ הֲמָסִ֗ים (oshb:Isa.64.1 = web:Isa.64.2, byte tier) and מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ גּוֹיִ֥ם יִרְגָּֽזוּ (oshb:Isa.64.1 = web:Isa.64.2, byte tier); web:Isa.64.3 (MT 64:2) carries the second mountain-quaking report יָרַ֕דְתָּ מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ הָרִ֥ים נָזֹֽלּוּ (oshb:Isa.64.2 = web:Isa.64.3, byte tier); and web:Isa.64.5 (MT 64:4) carries the confession הֵן אַתָּ֤ה קָצַ֨פְתָּ֙ וַֽנֶּחֱטָ֔א (oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, byte tier). Read as MT numbers they fail: oshb:Isa.64.3 = web:Isa.64.4 opens וּמֵעוֹלָ֥ם (oshb:Isa.64.3 = web:Isa.64.4, byte tier) and runs to the incomparability affirmation עַ֣יִן לֹֽא רָאָ֗תָה אֱלֹהִים֙ זוּלָ֣תְךָ֔ (oshb:Isa.64.3 = web:Isa.64.4, byte tier), not a quaking report, and MT 64:5 = web:Isa.64.6 is a different confession verse. So the defect is real: two zone-B coordinates in prose do not name their numbering space, against the rule that any digit touching chs 63-64 names it, in the row that carries the split verse and that otherwise dual-qualifies every structured ref. Tested the other way, against the finding: nothing in the row is byte-false, both coordinates resolve correctly under the governing convention, the row's boundary_evidence_refs and device_notes carry arithmetically correct duals, and no seam depends on either coordinate; the ambiguity is one of labeling, which the severity law places at low (disclosure shortfall), not a defective digit claim. Noted without effect on the verdict: the finding's own Hebrew citations are unfilled percent-s placeholders, so its byte grounds were re-derived here rather than trusted. Downgraded to low.

Re-derived from bytes; every run below collates at byte tier. MT 64:4 (= web:Isa.64.5 by the crosswalk) carries its athnach (U+0591) on its seventh token יִזְכְּר֑וּךָ (oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, byte tier); the half before it, פָּגַ֤עְתָּ אֶת שָׂשׂ֙ וְעֹ֣שֵׂה צֶ֔דֶק בִּדְרָכֶ֖יךָ יִזְכְּר֑וּךָ (oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, byte tier), is a 2ms verb with 2ms suffixes continuing the address to Yahweh from עַ֣יִן לֹֽא רָאָ֗תָה אֱלֹהִים֙ זוּלָ֣תְךָ֔ (oshb:Isa.64.3 = web:Isa.64.4, byte tier), rendered “You meet him who rejoices and does righteousness, those who remember you in your ways.” (web:Isa.64.5); the self-accusation הֵן אַתָּ֤ה קָצַ֨פְתָּ֙ וַֽנֶּחֱטָ֔א (oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, byte tier), whose וַֽנֶּחֱטָ֔א (oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, byte tier) is the verse's first first-person-plural form, stands only after that caesura, rendered “Behold, you were angry, and we sinned.” (web:Isa.64.5). The row closes 'immediately before the confessional turn ... (web:Isa.64.5) opens a different speech-act' and its rejected alternative treats 'the confessional turn at 64:5' as the whole verse's mode, so the rear-seam driver is presented as verse-initial when half a verse of the row's own second-person petition mode intervenes between the row's close and the turn; the book-order neighbor row discloses the mid-verse onset explicitly and this row does not. Tested the other way, against the finding: rows are verse-granular, web:Isa.64.4 = oshb:Isa.64.3 is the nearest verse boundary before the turn, and the paragraph-mark inventory carries no mark at MT 64:3 or 64:4, so the placement stands and no respan is implied; the defect is a mis-presented driver position in a medium_low, frontier-flagged row whose seam is argued from exactly that rhetorical-mode shift, a defective warrant not alone load-bearing: medium as filed.
